title: Relationships Between Models
description: Connect models with ForeignKey, ManyToManyField, and OneToOneField.

slides.title: Types of Relationships 🔗
slides.content:
## Three main relationships:

1. **Many‑to‑One** (Foreign Key) – A blog post has one author, an author can have many posts.
2. **Many‑to‑Many** – A post can have many tags, a tag can be on many posts.
3. **One‑to‑One** – A user has one profile, a profile belongs to one user.

Django provides specific fields for each.

slides.title: Foreign Key (Many‑to‑One)
slides.content: Add a reference to another model using `models.ForeignKey`.
slides.codeSnippet:
from django.db import models
from django.contrib.auth.models import User

class Post(models.Model):
    author = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    title = models.CharField(max_length=200)

# CASCADE means: if author deleted, delete all their posts.
# Other options: PROTECT, SET_NULL, etc.

quizData.question: Which field type would you use to model a one‑to‑many relationship (e.g., a category has many products)?
quizData.explanation: ForeignKey creates a many‑to‑one relationship. The model with the ForeignKey is the 'many' side.

slides.title: Many‑to‑Many Relationship
One‑to‑One Relationship
slides.content: Used for extending a built‑in model or for strict one‑to‑one mapping.
slides.codeSnippet:
class Profile(models.Model):
    user = models.OneToOneField(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE)
    bio = models.TextField(blank=True)
    location = models.CharField(max_length=100, blank=True)

slides.title: Accessing Related Objects
slides.codeSnippet:
# Forward: post.author gives the User object
post = Post.objects.get(id=1)
print(post.author.username)

# Reverse: user.post_set gives a QuerySet of all posts by that user
user = User.objects.get(username='john')
posts = user.post_set.all()

# You can set related_name to change the default `_set` name:
class Post(models.Model):
    author = models.ForeignKey(User, on_delete=models.CASCADE, related_name='blog_posts')
# Then use user.blog_posts.all()

slides.title: Pro Tip 💡
slides.content:
## Always set `on_delete`

Django requires `on_delete` for ForeignKey and OneToOneField. Choose the appropriate behavior (`CASCADE`, `PROTECT`, `SET_NULL`, etc.) to maintain data integrity.
